sentences.1: The dockyard clerk read through the harbourmaster's log for the week.
sentences.2: In it, the harbourmaster had written that the trawler crossed the bar early because the tide had turned.
sentences.3: The log went on to list who had crewed the boat and how much the catch had weighed.
sentences.4: The clerk also noted, from her own count, that six boats had tied up before noon.
sentences.5: The rest of the entry concerned repairs due on the north pier.

readings_chosen: Sentence 2: 'the harbourmaster had written that' — the readings open to me are that the writing is an actual past event, or that it is merely the framing of reported content (as 'the account says' is in the guide's first example). Chosen: the writing is an actual CLAIMED fact — a doer and a thing written in — while the reported clause is TOLD in log_world; the narrator endorses the writing, not the trawler claim.

Sentence 2: 'because the tide had turned' — the causal claim may be the narrator's or the log's. Chosen: the log's — the BECAUSE is TOLD in log_world and points at the told facts crossed and turned; no general MAKES rule is added, since that would make the claim its own premise.

Sentence 3: 'the boat' — this may be the same vessel as the trawler of sentence 2, or another boat. Chosen: kept apart as its own thing, because sentence 2 is the log's reported content and sentence 3 the narrator's summary, and the text does not say they are the same.

Sentence 3: 'The log went on to list who… and how much…' — the listed items may be the log's content (TOLD in log_world) or the narrator's commitment about the log (CLAIMED). Chosen: the narrator's summary — CLAIMED facts about what the log lists — with the values (who crewed, how much it weighed) sent to the bin as identity and quantity.

Sentence 4: 'The clerk also noted, from her own count, that six boats had tied up before noon' — the narrator may be asserting the tying-up, or only the clerk's noting of it. Chosen: the clerk's noting — the attribution goes to the bin and the content is TOLD in clerk_world. Unlike sentence 2's 'had written', which is an act upon a thing, 'noted, from her own count' is an attribution of observation, and the rules send such attributions to the bin.

Sentence 5: 'the entry' — this may be the same record as the log, or a separate entry. Chosen: kept apart as its own thing, so that only the entry, not the whole log, is said to concern repairs; 'the rest of' is binned as a portion.

Sentences 1, 2 and 4: 'read', 'wrote', 'crossed', 'turned' and 'tied up' have no shape in the shape book (no press, release or hold). Chosen: written as eventive facts (holds(read(clerk, log)) and the like) after the precedent of the reported opening in the guide's first example, so that no unchecked physical-verb happening is put before the checker.
